findings.label: Trip, terminal, and timing context
limits: These facts select assessment scope; they do not establish dispatch, route, or entry clearance.

The catalog's terminal-specific evidence supports APM Elizabeth only. A missing terminal leaves applicability unresolved, and another terminal creates an unsupported-terminal coverage gap rather than an exemption.
The NJPASS-hosted route-review clause is retained evidence, but its official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

findings.label: Gross, axle, and spacing evidence
limits: The federal clause is limited to the Interstate system and reasonable access; the New Jersey single-axle clause is limited to non-Interstate New Jersey roads.
Which limit applies depends on the exact roadway jurisdiction and route. This catalog implements no bridge-formula, axle-group, tire-load, or legal-weight calculator.
Gross weight, axle count, and reported axle weights or spacings do not by themselves establish compliance.
The NJPASS-hosted route-review clause is excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

findings.label: Loaded dimensions and exact route access
limits: Width limits depend on route-network status, and the cited local-access rule is expressly limited to a 102-inch-wide standard truck using unrestricted local roads by the direct route.
A road's absence from a listed network or restriction table establishes neither permission nor prohibition. Current local postings and every segment still require verification.
Published terminal directions and stored route topology are not legal route designation, bridge-clearance evidence, or navigable truck-route approval.

findings.label: Permit type and load eligibility evidence
limits: Permit applicability depends on the load, dimensions, axle facts, trip time, and permit terms; no legal interpretation or permit-validity check is implemented.
The ocean-container sources concern sealed ocean-borne containers and do not make every container move eligible for that permit type.
The NJPASS-hosted permit clause is retained but excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently archived and compared.
A reported permit, including a reported-valid permit, is user-reported evidence and does not establish approval or route coverage.

findings.label: Cross-authority route and permit coverage
limits: A New Jersey State permit does not establish approval for toll, county, local, Port Authority, or terminal-controlled segments.
Every reported approval requires verification from the responsible authority; a complete set of user reports is not cross-authority clearance.
The retained toll-road approval clause is excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

findings.label: Current route postings and operating conditions
limits: No live current-policy, posting, closure, lane, detour, escort, or route-condition integration is implemented.
The archived Port Street bulletin is a quarantined dated observation, not a source clause or proof of conditions on the trip date; it must be rechecked before operational use.
A user-reported check time does not verify the result, authority, route coverage, or continued currentness of that check.

findings.label: DTR registration and vehicle RFID evidence
limits: No live PortTruckPass, DTR, ownership-amendment, or RFID lookup is implemented.
Reported DTR or RFID status is not registry verification and does not establish terminal entry.

findings.label: DTR engine-policy evidence and retained tariff conflict
limits: The release preserves an unresolved internal tension between Subrules 34-1101 and 34-1140; the deadline clause is explicitly excluded from verified use.
This catalog does not reconcile the tariff, infer enforcement, or categorically approve or deny a truck from engine model year alone.
The 2014 engine language concerns completing DTR registration and must not be silently converted into a universal terminal-entry rule.

findings.label: Driver TWIC evidence
limits: The federal clause concerns unescorted access to regulated secure areas and retains its stated exceptions; this catalog does not determine whether an exception applies.
No live TSA or Port Authority credential verification is implemented. A reported TWIC is not verified access authorization.

findings.label: SeaLink and TWIC registration evidence
limits: No live SeaLink or TWIC-registration lookup is implemented.
Possession of an identifier and a reported registration do not establish current validity or terminal entry.

findings.label: APM safety induction tied to the current SeaLink
limits: This is the only catalog requirement with an implemented check, and it uses server-owned synthetic evidence rather than a live training provider.
A matching synthetic result addresses only induction for the current SeaLink; it is not dispatch, route, permit, or terminal-entry clearance.
Archived policy is not verified as current for the trip, and synthetic assessment dates do not create a training-expiry rule.

Synthetic evidence assessment dates are test controls, not a training expiry rule.
An out-of-scope check does not mean the person is exempt from other requirements.

findings.label: APM gate appointment evidence
limits: No live TERMPoint or terminal appointment lookup is implemented.
A reported appointment does not establish that it is current, matches this movement, or will be accepted at the gate.

findings.label: Same-day transaction and gate release evidence
limits: The pinned release contains no retained source clause that establishes same-day transaction or gate-release requirements.
No live terminal transaction, gate, cargo-release, or admission integration is implemented. Reported release status cannot establish entry.
Synthetic development cases only; no operational entry or dispatch clearance.
Reported facts are not authoritative verification, even when a reporter says verified.

queries.cypher: MATCH (r:DrayageRelease {dataset:$dataset, revision:$revision}) RETURN r.manifest_json AS manifest
MATCH (n:DrayageRecord {dataset:$dataset, revision:$revision}) RETURN n{.id,.kind,.layer,.archive,.ordinal,.record_json} AS node ORDER BY n.ordinal

MATCH (a:DrayageRecord {dataset:$dataset, revision:$revision})-[e]->(b:DrayageRecord {dataset:$dataset, revision:$revision}) WHERE e.dataset=$dataset AND e.revision=$revision RETURN {id:e.id, from:a.id, to:b.id, relationship:type(e), archive:e.archive, ordinal:e.ordinal, record_json:e.record_json} AS edge ORDER BY e.ordinal
MATCH (n:DrayageRecord {dataset:$dataset, revision:$revision, id:$id}) RETURN n.kind AS kind, n.layer AS layer, n.archive AS archive, n.record_json AS record

MATCH (n:DrayageRecord {dataset:$dataset, revision:$revision, id:$id}) MATCH (n)-[e]->(other) WHERE other:DrayageRecord AND other.dataset=$dataset AND other.revision=$revision AND e.dataset=$dataset AND e.revision=$revision AND type(e)=$relationship RETURN other.id AS id ORDER BY id

MATCH (n:DrayageRecord {dataset:$dataset, revision:$revision, id:$id}) MATCH (n)-[e]->(other) WHERE other:DrayageRecord AND other.dataset=$dataset AND other.revision=$revision AND e.dataset=$dataset AND e.revision=$revision AND type(e)=$relationship RETURN other.id AS id ORDER BY id

MATCH (n:DrayageRecord {dataset:$dataset, revision:$revision, id:$id}) RETURN n.kind AS kind, n.layer AS layer, n.archive AS archive, n.record_json AS record

findings.label: Trip, terminal, and timing context
limits: These facts select assessment scope; they do not establish dispatch, route, or entry clearance.

The catalog's terminal-specific evidence supports APM Elizabeth only. A missing terminal leaves applicability unresolved, and another terminal creates an unsupported-terminal coverage gap rather than an exemption.
The NJPASS-hosted route-review clause is retained evidence, but its official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

findings.label: Gross, axle, and spacing evidence
limits: The federal clause is limited to the Interstate system and reasonable access; the New Jersey single-axle clause is limited to non-Interstate New Jersey roads.
Which limit applies depends on the exact roadway jurisdiction and route. This catalog implements no bridge-formula, axle-group, tire-load, or legal-weight calculator.
Gross weight, axle count, and reported axle weights or spacings do not by themselves establish compliance.
The NJPASS-hosted route-review clause is excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

findings.label: Loaded dimensions and exact route access
limits: Width limits depend on route-network status, and the cited local-access rule is expressly limited to a 102-inch-wide standard truck using unrestricted local roads by the direct route.
A road's absence from a listed network or restriction table establishes neither permission nor prohibition. Current local postings and every segment still require verification.
Published terminal directions and stored route topology are not legal route designation, bridge-clearance evidence, or navigable truck-route approval.

findings.label: Permit type and load eligibility evidence
limits: Permit applicability depends on the load, dimensions, axle facts, trip time, and permit terms; no legal interpretation or permit-validity check is implemented.
The ocean-container sources concern sealed ocean-borne containers and do not make every container move eligible for that permit type.
The NJPASS-hosted permit clause is retained but excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently archived and compared.
A reported permit, including a reported-valid permit, is user-reported evidence and does not establish approval or route coverage.

findings.label: Cross-authority route and permit coverage
limits: A New Jersey State permit does not establish approval for toll, county, local, Port Authority, or terminal-controlled segments.
Every reported approval requires verification from the responsible authority; a complete set of user reports is not cross-authority clearance.
The retained toll-road approval clause is excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

findings.label: Current route postings and operating conditions
limits: No live current-policy, posting, closure, lane, detour, escort, or route-condition integration is implemented.
The archived Port Street bulletin is a quarantined dated observation, not a source clause or proof of conditions on the trip date; it must be rechecked before operational use.
A user-reported check time does not verify the result, authority, route coverage, or continued currentness of that check.

findings.label: DTR registration and vehicle RFID evidence
limits: No live PortTruckPass, DTR, ownership-amendment, or RFID lookup is implemented.
Reported DTR or RFID status is not registry verification and does not establish terminal entry.

findings.label: DTR engine-policy evidence and retained tariff conflict
limits: The release preserves an unresolved internal tension between Subrules 34-1101 and 34-1140; the deadline clause is explicitly excluded from verified use.
This catalog does not reconcile the tariff, infer enforcement, or categorically approve or deny a truck from engine model year alone.
The 2014 engine language concerns completing DTR registration and must not be silently converted into a universal terminal-entry rule.

findings.label: Driver TWIC evidence
limits: The federal clause concerns unescorted access to regulated secure areas and retains its stated exceptions; this catalog does not determine whether an exception applies.
No live TSA or Port Authority credential verification is implemented. A reported TWIC is not verified access authorization.

findings.label: SeaLink and TWIC registration evidence
limits: No live SeaLink or TWIC-registration lookup is implemented.
Possession of an identifier and a reported registration do not establish current validity or terminal entry.

findings.label: APM safety induction tied to the current SeaLink
limits: This is the only catalog requirement with an implemented check, and it uses server-owned synthetic evidence rather than a live training provider.
A matching synthetic result addresses only induction for the current SeaLink; it is not dispatch, route, permit, or terminal-entry clearance.
Archived policy is not verified as current for the trip, and synthetic assessment dates do not create a training-expiry rule.
No dispatch, entry, permit or route clearance is issued.
Archived policy has not been verified as current for this trip.
Synthetic evidence assessment dates are test controls, not a training expiry rule.
An out-of-scope check does not mean the person is exempt from other requirements.

findings.label: APM gate appointment evidence
limits: No live TERMPoint or terminal appointment lookup is implemented.
A reported appointment does not establish that it is current, matches this movement, or will be accepted at the gate.

findings.label: Same-day transaction and gate release evidence
limits: The pinned release contains no retained source clause that establishes same-day transaction or gate-release requirements.
No live terminal transaction, gate, cargo-release, or admission integration is implemented. Reported release status cannot establish entry.
Synthetic development cases only; no operational entry or dispatch clearance.
Reported facts are not authoritative verification, even when a reporter says verified.
The catalog is incomplete; current policy, CDL, gate state and other duties remain outside executable coverage.
Archived directions and bulletins do not establish legal access or current road conditions.
Only APM induction has an executable evaluator, using server-owned synthetic fixtures.

queries.cypher: MATCH (r:DrayageRelease {dataset:$dataset, revision:$revision}) RETURN r.manifest_json AS manifest
MATCH (n:DrayageRecord {dataset:$dataset, revision:$revision}) RETURN n{.id,.kind,.layer,.archive,.ordinal,.record_json} AS node ORDER BY n.ordinal

MATCH (a:DrayageRecord {dataset:$dataset, revision:$revision})-[e]->(b:DrayageRecord {dataset:$dataset, revision:$revision}) WHERE e.dataset=$dataset AND e.revision=$revision RETURN {id:e.id, from:a.id, to:b.id, relationship:type(e), archive:e.archive, ordinal:e.ordinal, record_json:e.record_json} AS edge ORDER BY e.ordinal
MATCH (n:DrayageRecord {dataset:$dataset, revision:$revision, id:$id}) RETURN n.kind AS kind, n.layer AS layer, n.archive AS archive, n.record_json AS record

MATCH (n:DrayageRecord {dataset:$dataset, revision:$revision, id:$id}) MATCH (n)-[e]->(other) WHERE other:DrayageRecord AND other.dataset=$dataset AND other.revision=$revision AND e.dataset=$dataset AND e.revision=$revision AND type(e)=$relationship RETURN other.id AS id ORDER BY id

MATCH (n:DrayageRecord {dataset:$dataset, revision:$revision, id:$id}) MATCH (n)-[e]->(other) WHERE other:DrayageRecord AND other.dataset=$dataset AND other.revision=$revision AND e.dataset=$dataset AND e.revision=$revision AND type(e)=$relationship RETURN other.id AS id ORDER BY id

MATCH (n:DrayageRecord {dataset:$dataset, revision:$revision, id:$id}) MATCH (n)<-[e]-(other) WHERE other:DrayageRecord AND other.dataset=$dataset AND other.revision=$revision AND e.dataset=$dataset AND e.revision=$revision AND type(e)=$relationship RETURN other.id AS id ORDER BY id
MATCH (n:DrayageRecord {dataset:$dataset, revision:$revision, id:$id}) RETURN n.kind AS kind, n.layer AS layer, n.archive AS archive, n.record_json AS record
MATCH (n:DrayageRecord {dataset:$dataset, revision:$revision, id:$id}) RETURN n.kind AS kind, n.layer AS layer, n.archive AS archive, n.record_json AS record

findings.label: Trip, terminal, and timing context
limits: These facts select assessment scope; they do not establish dispatch, route, or entry clearance.

The catalog's terminal-specific evidence supports APM Elizabeth only. A missing terminal leaves applicability unresolved, and another terminal creates an unsupported-terminal coverage gap rather than an exemption.
The NJPASS-hosted route-review clause is retained evidence, but its official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

findings.label: Gross, axle, and spacing evidence
limits: The federal clause is limited to the Interstate system and reasonable access; the New Jersey single-axle clause is limited to non-Interstate New Jersey roads.
Which limit applies depends on the exact roadway jurisdiction and route. This catalog implements no bridge-formula, axle-group, tire-load, or legal-weight calculator.
Gross weight, axle count, and reported axle weights or spacings do not by themselves establish compliance.
The NJPASS-hosted route-review clause is excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

findings.label: Loaded dimensions and exact route access
limits: Width limits depend on route-network status, and the cited local-access rule is expressly limited to a 102-inch-wide standard truck using unrestricted local roads by the direct route.
A road's absence from a listed network or restriction table establishes neither permission nor prohibition. Current local postings and every segment still require verification.
Published terminal directions and stored route topology are not legal route designation, bridge-clearance evidence, or navigable truck-route approval.

findings.label: Permit type and load eligibility evidence
limits: Permit applicability depends on the load, dimensions, axle facts, trip time, and permit terms; no legal interpretation or permit-validity check is implemented.
The ocean-container sources concern sealed ocean-borne containers and do not make every container move eligible for that permit type.
The NJPASS-hosted permit clause is retained but excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently archived and compared.
A reported permit, including a reported-valid permit, is user-reported evidence and does not establish approval or route coverage.

findings.label: Cross-authority route and permit coverage
limits: A New Jersey State permit does not establish approval for toll, county, local, Port Authority, or terminal-controlled segments.
Every reported approval requires verification from the responsible authority; a complete set of user reports is not cross-authority clearance.
The retained toll-road approval clause is excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

findings.label: Current route postings and operating conditions
limits: No live current-policy, posting, closure, lane, detour, escort, or route-condition integration is implemented.
The archived Port Street bulletin is a quarantined dated observation, not a source clause or proof of conditions on the trip date; it must be rechecked before operational use.
A user-reported check time does not verify the result, authority, route coverage, or continued currentness of that check.

findings.label: DTR registration and vehicle RFID evidence
limits: No live PortTruckPass, DTR, ownership-amendment, or RFID lookup is implemented.
Reported DTR or RFID status is not registry verification and does not establish terminal entry.

findings.label: DTR engine-policy evidence and retained tariff conflict
limits: The release preserves an unresolved internal tension between Subrules 34-1101 and 34-1140; the deadline clause is explicitly excluded from verified use.
This catalog does not reconcile the tariff, infer enforcement, or categorically approve or deny a truck from engine model year alone.
The 2014 engine language concerns completing DTR registration and must not be silently converted into a universal terminal-entry rule.

findings.label: Driver TWIC evidence
limits: The federal clause concerns unescorted access to regulated secure areas and retains its stated exceptions; this catalog does not determine whether an exception applies.
No live TSA or Port Authority credential verification is implemented. A reported TWIC is not verified access authorization.

findings.label: SeaLink and TWIC registration evidence
limits: No live SeaLink or TWIC-registration lookup is implemented.
Possession of an identifier and a reported registration do not establish current validity or terminal entry.

findings.label: APM safety induction tied to the current SeaLink
limits: This is the only catalog requirement with an implemented check, and it uses server-owned synthetic evidence rather than a live training provider.
A matching synthetic result addresses only induction for the current SeaLink; it is not dispatch, route, permit, or terminal-entry clearance.
Archived policy is not verified as current for the trip, and synthetic assessment dates do not create a training-expiry rule.
No dispatch, entry, permit or route clearance is issued.
Archived policy has not been verified as current for this trip.
Synthetic evidence assessment dates are test controls, not a training expiry rule.
An out-of-scope check does not mean the person is exempt from other requirements.

findings.label: APM gate appointment evidence
limits: No live TERMPoint or terminal appointment lookup is implemented.
A reported appointment does not establish that it is current, matches this movement, or will be accepted at the gate.

findings.label: Same-day transaction and gate release evidence
limits: The pinned release contains no retained source clause that establishes same-day transaction or gate-release requirements.
No live terminal transaction, gate, cargo-release, or admission integration is implemented. Reported release status cannot establish entry.
Synthetic development cases only; no operational entry or dispatch clearance.
Reported facts are not authoritative verification, even when a reporter says verified.
The catalog is incomplete; current policy, CDL, gate state and other duties remain outside executable coverage.
Archived directions and bulletins do not establish legal access or current road conditions.
Only APM induction has an executable evaluator, using server-owned synthetic fixtures.

The details of the anticipated route of travel, including locations of the entrance to and exit from the New Jersey State highway system, including, but not limited to, the interstate highways, the New Jersey Turnpike, the Garden State Parkway south of Exit 105 and the Atlantic City Expressway; and
(d) Applications for single-trip permits will be reviewed for acceptability of the route being used in conjunction with the vehicle's load and axle configuration.

(e) Applications for single-trip permits will be rejected where the vehicle's load and axle configuration overstress the structures being crossed on the anticipated route of travel. Rejected applications will identify the structures on the proposed route being overstressed. Applicants can either modify the vehicle's load, weight over each axle or axle spacing to lessen the load impact or choose an alternative route. Applicants can contact the New Jersey Department of Transportation, Bureau of Structural Engineering at 609-530-2579 for assistance in the choice of acceptable alternative routes.

structuredContent.label: Gross, axle, and spacing evidence
limits: The federal clause is limited to the Interstate system and reasonable access; the New Jersey single-axle clause is limited to non-Interstate New Jersey roads.
Which limit applies depends on the exact roadway jurisdiction and route. This catalog implements no bridge-formula, axle-group, tire-load, or legal-weight calculator.
Gross weight, axle count, and reported axle weights or spacings do not by themselves establish compliance.
The NJPASS-hosted route-review clause is excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

sources.publisher: Office of the Federal Register / Government Publishing Office
source_text: (a) The provisions of the section are applicable to the National System of Interstate and Defense Highways and reasonable access thereto.
(b) The maximum gross vehicle weight shall be 80,000 pounds except where lower gross vehicle weight is dictated by the bridge formula.
(c) The maximum gross weight upon any one axle, including any one axle of a group of axles, or a vehicle is 20,000 pounds.
(d) The maximum gross weight on tandem axles is 34,000 pounds.

(e) No vehicle or combination of vehicles shall be moved or operated on any Interstate highway when the gross weight on two or more consecutive axles exceeds the limitations prescribed by the following formula, referred to as the Bridge Gross Weight Formula:
sources.title: 23 CFR 658.17 — Weight

sources.publisher: New Jersey Department of Transportation
sources.source_text: The maximum weight allowed on a signle axle is 22,400 lbs.
sources.title: NJ Commercial Vehicle Size and Weight Guidebook

sources.publisher: New Jersey Department of Transportation
source_text: The maximum weight allowed on axle group of this type is 34,000 lbs.
The gross vehicle weight is defined as a vehicle or combination of vehicles, including load or contents. The maximum overall gross weight of a vehicle is 80,000 lbs., as shown in the diagram above.

NOTE: Compliance with bridge formula weight limits may require axle weights lower than the standard weight limits of 34,000 pounds for a tandem axle set and a gross weight lower than the standard 80,000-pound limit.
sources.title: NJ Commercial Vehicle Size and Weight Guidebook

source_text: 3. The vehicle height, length and width;
4. The axle configuration and weight over each axle;
5. The overall gross vehicle weight;
6. The dates of travel;

7. The details of the anticipated route of travel, including locations of the entrance to and exit from the New Jersey State highway system, including, but not limited to, the interstate highways, the New Jersey Turnpike, the Garden State Parkway south of Exit 105 and the Atlantic City Expressway; and
(d) Applications for single-trip permits will be reviewed for acceptability of the route being used in conjunction with the vehicle's load and axle configuration.

(e) Applications for single-trip permits will be rejected where the vehicle's load and axle configuration overstress the structures being crossed on the anticipated route of travel. Rejected applications will identify the structures on the proposed route being overstressed. Applicants can either modify the vehicle's load, weight over each axle or axle spacing to lessen the load impact or choose an alternative route. Applicants can contact the New Jersey Department of Transportation, Bureau of Structural Engineering at 609-530-2579 for assistance in the choice of acceptable alternative routes.

structuredContent.label: Loaded dimensions and exact route access
limits: Width limits depend on route-network status, and the cited local-access rule is expressly limited to a 102-inch-wide standard truck using unrestricted local roads by the direct route.
A road's absence from a listed network or restriction table establishes neither permission nor prohibition. Current local postings and every segment still require verification.
Published terminal directions and stored route topology are not legal route designation, bridge-clearance evidence, or navigable truck-route approval.

sources.publisher: New Jersey Department of Transportation
source_text: Width 96 inches on routes that are not National Network or NJ Access Routes 102 inches on National Network and NJ Access Routes

As the diagram above shows, the maximum width of a commercial vehicle traveling within the State of New Jersey is 102 inches (or 8 feet 6 inches). In some instances, rules and regulations may be promulgated for those public roads, streets or highways or public or quasi-public property in this State, where it is determined that the interests of public safety and welfare require the maximum outside width be no more than 96 inches.
sources.title: NJ Commercial Vehicle Size and Weight Guidebook

sources.publisher: New Jersey Department of Transportation
sources.source_text: The maximum height of any commercial vehicle or combination of vehicles, including load or contents of any part or portion thereof, traveling within the State of New Jersey is 13’-6” on all highways, except as otherwise identified, as shown in the height diagram above.
sources.title: NJ Commercial Vehicle Size and Weight Guidebook

sources.publisher: New Jersey Department of Transportation
source_text: As the diagram above shows, the maximum length of a semitrailer shall not exceed 53 feet when operated as part of a combination of vehicles consisting of one motor-drawn vehicle and a drawing or power unit vehicle.

Semitrailers greater than 48 feet in length but not more than 53 feet in length must be transported using the National Network unless seeking food, fuel, rest, repairs or to reach a terminal by the direct route (that is, the shortest travel distance). Upon completing each trip, the large truck should return to the National Network in a manner consistent with reaching its next terminal. Trips off of the National Network or the New Jersey Access Network onto all other local unrestricted roadways should only be for the purpose of accessing a terminal on those roadways, by the shortest distance.
sources.title: NJ Commercial Vehicle Size and Weight Guidebook

An example of such a restriction is a maximum weight posting or the designation of local "truck route" restrictions that have been adopted and posted as provided at N.J.S.A. 40:67-16.1 et seq.

structuredContent.label: Permit type and load eligibility evidence
limits: Permit applicability depends on the load, dimensions, axle facts, trip time, and permit terms; no legal interpretation or permit-validity check is implemented.
The ocean-container sources concern sealed ocean-borne containers and do not make every container move eligible for that permit type.
The NJPASS-hosted permit clause is retained but excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently archived and compared.
A reported permit, including a reported-valid permit, is user-reported evidence and does not establish approval or route coverage.

sources.publisher: New Jersey Motor Vehicle Commission; hosted by the New Jersey Department of Transportation NJPASS system
source_text: (a) Except as provided in (c) below, a single-trip permit is required for each one-way trip of an oversize or overweight vehicle that exceeds the dimension or weight provisions of N.J.S.A. 39:3-84.
(b) In the event the vehicle is both oversize and overweight, a single-trip permit will be issued for each one-way trip.

(c) An annual ocean borne containerized cargo multiple-trip permit may be issued for a tractor semitrailer combination engaged in the transportation of sealed containers of the type commonly used for the conveyance of freight transportation in international ocean going commerce as follows:

1. Sealed containers transported under an annual ocean borne containerized cargo multiple-trip permit shall bear the seal of the United States Custom Service, the seal of another governmental agency or the seal of a shipper;

2. The combined gross vehicle weight of any tractor semitrailer combination, including load or content conveying sealed containers, shall not exceed 90,000 pounds. The tractor semitrailer combination per-axle combined weight shall not exceed 38,000 pounds for any one tandem axle unit in any tractor semitrailer combination and shall not exceed 56,400 pounds for any tri-axle trailer configuration. Additionally, vehicles shall conform with the axle limitations in N.J.S.A. 39:3-84 and the maximum tire load limit in N.J.A.C. 13:18-1.10(a)2. Vehicles or combination of vehicles that exceed these weight limits may not use an annual ocean borne containerized cargo multiple-trip permit and shall obtain a single-trip permit as described in (a) above;
sources.title: N.J.A.C. 13:18, Subchapter 1 — Permits for Overdimensional or Overweight Vehicles

sources.publisher: New Jersey Department of Transportation
sources.source_text: A single-trip permit allows a carrier to haul a non-divisible load above legal size and/or weight limitations and is valid for a single trip within a period of five days. In the event the one-way trip cannot be completed within the valid life of the single-trip permit due to hazardous road conditions or vehicle breakdown, a one-day extension may be granted provided that the request is made to the DOT before the permit has expired. Permit restrictions are assigned based on requested dimensions and weights.
sources.title: NJ Commercial Vehicle Size and Weight Guidebook

sources.publisher: New Jersey Department of Transportation
source_text: An Ocean Borne Container Permit can be obtained for a truck tractor semitrailer combination engaged in the overweight transportation of sealed containers of the type commonly used for the conveyance of freight transportation in international ocean-going commerce. Moves made under this permit type must be of legal dimensions and are subject to the weight limitations shown in Table 5.
TABLE 5 OCEAN BORNE CONTAINER PERMIT WEIGHT LIMITATIONS: Maximum Gross Weight 90,000 lbs; Maximum Tandem Weight 38,000 lbs; Maximum Tri-axle Weight 56,400 lbs.
sources.title: NJ Commercial Vehicle Size and Weight Guidebook

structuredContent.label: Cross-authority route and permit coverage
limits: A New Jersey State permit does not establish approval for toll, county, local, Port Authority, or terminal-controlled segments.
Every reported approval requires verification from the responsible authority; a complete set of user reports is not cross-authority clearance.
The retained toll-road approval clause is excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

sources.publisher: New Jersey Motor Vehicle Commission; hosted by the New Jersey Department of Transportation NJPASS system
sources.source_text: 2. On any toll road, without the express approval of the tolling authority, including, but not limited to, the South Jersey Transportation Authority for the Atlantic City Expressway; and the New Jersey Turnpike Authority for the New Jersey Turnpike and the Garden State Parkway;
sources.title: N.J.A.C. 13:18, Subchapter 1 — Permits for Overdimensional or Overweight Vehicles

sources.publisher: New Jersey Department of Transportation
sources.source_text: The rules of this chapter do not supersede other State rules outside of this chapter, municipal ordinances, and county resolutions, which may otherwise restrict or control the through-movements of trucks or other vehicles. An example of such a restriction is a maximum weight posting or the designation of local "truck route" restrictions that have been adopted and posted as provided at N.J.S.A. 40:67-16.1 et seq.
sources.title: N.J.A.C. 16:32 — Truck Access

sources.publisher: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey
source_text: All persons on any air terminal highway or marine terminal highway must at all times comply with any lawful order, signal or direction by voice or hand of any member of the Port Authority police force. When traffic is controlled by traffic lights, signs or by mechanical or electrical signals, such lights, signs and signals shall be obeyed unless a Port Authority police officer directs otherwise.

Unless otherwise directed, all vehicles on any air terminal highway or marine terminal highway shall at all times stay to the right of the center of the roadway, except in the case of one-way roadways; slow- moving vehicles shall remain as close as possible to the right-hand edge or curb of the roadway; and where a roadway is marked with traffic lanes, vehicles shall not cross markings.

No person shall operate a motor vehicle on an air terminal highway or marine terminal highway unless he is duly authorized to operate such vehicle on State and municipal highways in the State in which such air terminal highway or marine terminal highway is located, or unless he is especially authorized by the Port Authority to operate motor vehicles on such air terminal highway or marine terminal highway. No motor vehicle shall be permitted on any air terminal highway or marine terminal highway unless it is registered in accordance with the provisions of the law of the State in which such air terminal highway or marine terminal highway is located, or unless it is especially authorized by the Port Authority to be operated on such air terminal highway or marine terminal highway.
sources.title: Port Authority Marine Terminal Tariff FMC Schedule No. PA-10

sources.publisher: New Jersey Department of Transportation
sources.source_text: The rules of this chapter do not supersede other State rules outside of this chapter, municipal ordinances, and county resolutions, which may otherwise restrict or control the through-movements of trucks or other vehicles. An example of such a restriction is a maximum weight posting or the designation of local "truck route" restrictions that have been adopted and posted as provided at N.J.S.A. 40:67-16.1 et seq.
sources.title: N.J.A.C. 16:32 — Truck Access

sources.publisher: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey
source_text: All persons on any air terminal highway or marine terminal highway must at all times comply with any lawful order, signal or direction by voice or hand of any member of the Port Authority police force. When traffic is controlled by traffic lights, signs or by mechanical or electrical signals, such lights, signs and signals shall be obeyed unless a Port Authority police officer directs otherwise.

Unless otherwise directed, all vehicles on any air terminal highway or marine terminal highway shall at all times stay to the right of the center of the roadway, except in the case of one-way roadways; slow- moving vehicles shall remain as close as possible to the right-hand edge or curb of the roadway; and where a roadway is marked with traffic lanes, vehicles shall not cross markings.

No person shall operate a motor vehicle on an air terminal highway or marine terminal highway unless he is duly authorized to operate such vehicle on State and municipal highways in the State in which such air terminal highway or marine terminal highway is located, or unless he is especially authorized by the Port Authority to operate motor vehicles on such air terminal highway or marine terminal highway. No motor vehicle shall be permitted on any air terminal highway or marine terminal highway unless it is registered in accordance with the provisions of the law of the State in which such air terminal highway or marine terminal highway is located, or unless it is especially authorized by the Port Authority to be operated on such air terminal highway or marine terminal highway.
sources.title: Port Authority Marine Terminal Tariff FMC Schedule No. PA-10

sources.publisher: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey
sources.source_text: All Drayage Trucks seeking entry onto any Port Authority Terminal shall be registered in the DTR prior to the date of entry. Registration in the DTR shall be in electronic format via the PortTruckPass (PTP) website (www.porttruckpass.com). In the event of a change to the information provided for registration in the DTR with respect to a registered vehicle, such information shall be amended within ten (10) calendar days of the change via the PortTruckPass website (www.porttruckpass.com). Supporting documentation may be required for verification purposes with regard to registration or amendment.
sources.title: Port Authority Marine Terminal Tariff FMC Schedule No. PA-10

sources.publisher: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey
source_text: All Class 8 drayage trucks seeking entry onto any Port of New York and New Jersey Marine Terminal must be registered in the Drayage Truck Registry (DTR) and have a valid RFID tag properly mounted on the vehicle.
No tag, no entry.

findings.label: Trip, terminal, and timing context
limits: These facts select assessment scope; they do not establish dispatch, route, or entry clearance.

The catalog's terminal-specific evidence supports APM Elizabeth only. A missing terminal leaves applicability unresolved, and another terminal creates an unsupported-terminal coverage gap rather than an exemption.
The NJPASS-hosted route-review clause is retained evidence, but its official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

findings.label: Gross, axle, and spacing evidence
limits: The federal clause is limited to the Interstate system and reasonable access; the New Jersey single-axle clause is limited to non-Interstate New Jersey roads.
Which limit applies depends on the exact roadway jurisdiction and route. This catalog implements no bridge-formula, axle-group, tire-load, or legal-weight calculator.
Gross weight, axle count, and reported axle weights or spacings do not by themselves establish compliance.
The NJPASS-hosted route-review clause is excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

findings.label: Loaded dimensions and exact route access
limits: Width limits depend on route-network status, and the cited local-access rule is expressly limited to a 102-inch-wide standard truck using unrestricted local roads by the direct route.
A road's absence from a listed network or restriction table establishes neither permission nor prohibition. Current local postings and every segment still require verification.
Published terminal directions and stored route topology are not legal route designation, bridge-clearance evidence, or navigable truck-route approval.

findings.label: Permit type and load eligibility evidence
limits: Permit applicability depends on the load, dimensions, axle facts, trip time, and permit terms; no legal interpretation or permit-validity check is implemented.
The ocean-container sources concern sealed ocean-borne containers and do not make every container move eligible for that permit type.
The NJPASS-hosted permit clause is retained but excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently archived and compared.
A reported permit, including a reported-valid permit, is user-reported evidence and does not establish approval or route coverage.

findings.label: Cross-authority route and permit coverage
limits: A New Jersey State permit does not establish approval for toll, county, local, Port Authority, or terminal-controlled segments.
Every reported approval requires verification from the responsible authority; a complete set of user reports is not cross-authority clearance.
The retained toll-road approval clause is excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

findings.label: Current route postings and operating conditions
limits: No live current-policy, posting, closure, lane, detour, escort, or route-condition integration is implemented.
The archived Port Street bulletin is a quarantined dated observation, not a source clause or proof of conditions on the trip date; it must be rechecked before operational use.
A user-reported check time does not verify the result, authority, route coverage, or continued currentness of that check.

findings.label: DTR registration and vehicle RFID evidence
limits: No live PortTruckPass, DTR, ownership-amendment, or RFID lookup is implemented.
Reported DTR or RFID status is not registry verification and does not establish terminal entry.

findings.label: DTR engine-policy evidence and retained tariff conflict
limits: The release preserves an unresolved internal tension between Subrules 34-1101 and 34-1140; the deadline clause is explicitly excluded from verified use.
This catalog does not reconcile the tariff, infer enforcement, or categorically approve or deny a truck from engine model year alone.
The 2014 engine language concerns completing DTR registration and must not be silently converted into a universal terminal-entry rule.

findings.label: Driver TWIC evidence
limits: The federal clause concerns unescorted access to regulated secure areas and retains its stated exceptions; this catalog does not determine whether an exception applies.
No live TSA or Port Authority credential verification is implemented. A reported TWIC is not verified access authorization.

findings.label: SeaLink and TWIC registration evidence
limits: No live SeaLink or TWIC-registration lookup is implemented.
Possession of an identifier and a reported registration do not establish current validity or terminal entry.

findings.label: APM safety induction tied to the current SeaLink
limits: This is the only catalog requirement with an implemented check, and it uses server-owned synthetic evidence rather than a live training provider.
A matching synthetic result addresses only induction for the current SeaLink; it is not dispatch, route, permit, or terminal-entry clearance.
Archived policy is not verified as current for the trip, and synthetic assessment dates do not create a training-expiry rule.
No dispatch, entry, permit or route clearance is issued.
Archived policy has not been verified as current for this trip.
Synthetic evidence assessment dates are test controls, not a training expiry rule.
An out-of-scope check does not mean the person is exempt from other requirements.

findings.label: APM gate appointment evidence
limits: No live TERMPoint or terminal appointment lookup is implemented.
A reported appointment does not establish that it is current, matches this movement, or will be accepted at the gate.

findings.label: Same-day transaction and gate release evidence
limits: The pinned release contains no retained source clause that establishes same-day transaction or gate-release requirements.
No live terminal transaction, gate, cargo-release, or admission integration is implemented. Reported release status cannot establish entry.
Synthetic development cases only; no operational entry or dispatch clearance.
Reported facts are not authoritative verification, even when a reporter says verified.
The catalog is incomplete; current policy, CDL, gate state and other duties remain outside executable coverage.
Archived directions and bulletins do not establish legal access or current road conditions.
Only APM induction has an executable evaluator, using server-owned synthetic fixtures.

findings.label: Trip, terminal, and timing context
limits: These facts select assessment scope; they do not establish dispatch, route, or entry clearance.

The catalog's terminal-specific evidence supports APM Elizabeth only. A missing terminal leaves applicability unresolved, and another terminal creates an unsupported-terminal coverage gap rather than an exemption.
The NJPASS-hosted route-review clause is retained evidence, but its official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

findings.label: Gross, axle, and spacing evidence
limits: The federal clause is limited to the Interstate system and reasonable access; the New Jersey single-axle clause is limited to non-Interstate New Jersey roads.
Which limit applies depends on the exact roadway jurisdiction and route. This catalog implements no bridge-formula, axle-group, tire-load, or legal-weight calculator.
Gross weight, axle count, and reported axle weights or spacings do not by themselves establish compliance.
The NJPASS-hosted route-review clause is excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

findings.label: Loaded dimensions and exact route access
limits: Width limits depend on route-network status, and the cited local-access rule is expressly limited to a 102-inch-wide standard truck using unrestricted local roads by the direct route.
A road's absence from a listed network or restriction table establishes neither permission nor prohibition. Current local postings and every segment still require verification.
Published terminal directions and stored route topology are not legal route designation, bridge-clearance evidence, or navigable truck-route approval.

findings.label: Permit type and load eligibility evidence
limits: Permit applicability depends on the load, dimensions, axle facts, trip time, and permit terms; no legal interpretation or permit-validity check is implemented.
The ocean-container sources concern sealed ocean-borne containers and do not make every container move eligible for that permit type.
The NJPASS-hosted permit clause is retained but excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently archived and compared.
A reported permit, including a reported-valid permit, is user-reported evidence and does not establish approval or route coverage.

findings.label: Cross-authority route and permit coverage
limits: A New Jersey State permit does not establish approval for toll, county, local, Port Authority, or terminal-controlled segments.
Every reported approval requires verification from the responsible authority; a complete set of user reports is not cross-authority clearance.
The retained toll-road approval clause is excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

findings.label: Current route postings and operating conditions
limits: No live current-policy, posting, closure, lane, detour, escort, or route-condition integration is implemented.
The archived Port Street bulletin is a quarantined dated observation, not a source clause or proof of conditions on the trip date; it must be rechecked before operational use.
A user-reported check time does not verify the result, authority, route coverage, or continued currentness of that check.

findings.label: DTR registration and vehicle RFID evidence
limits: No live PortTruckPass, DTR, ownership-amendment, or RFID lookup is implemented.
Reported DTR or RFID status is not registry verification and does not establish terminal entry.

findings.label: DTR engine-policy evidence and retained tariff conflict
limits: The release preserves an unresolved internal tension between Subrules 34-1101 and 34-1140; the deadline clause is explicitly excluded from verified use.
This catalog does not reconcile the tariff, infer enforcement, or categorically approve or deny a truck from engine model year alone.
The 2014 engine language concerns completing DTR registration and must not be silently converted into a universal terminal-entry rule.

findings.label: Driver TWIC evidence
limits: The federal clause concerns unescorted access to regulated secure areas and retains its stated exceptions; this catalog does not determine whether an exception applies.
No live TSA or Port Authority credential verification is implemented. A reported TWIC is not verified access authorization.

findings.label: SeaLink and TWIC registration evidence
limits: No live SeaLink or TWIC-registration lookup is implemented.
Possession of an identifier and a reported registration do not establish current validity or terminal entry.

findings.label: APM safety induction tied to the current SeaLink
limits: This is the only catalog requirement with an implemented check, and it uses server-owned synthetic evidence rather than a live training provider.
A matching synthetic result addresses only induction for the current SeaLink; it is not dispatch, route, permit, or terminal-entry clearance.
Archived policy is not verified as current for the trip, and synthetic assessment dates do not create a training-expiry rule.
No dispatch, entry, permit or route clearance is issued.
Archived policy has not been verified as current for this trip.
Synthetic evidence assessment dates are test controls, not a training expiry rule.
An out-of-scope check does not mean the person is exempt from other requirements.

findings.label: APM gate appointment evidence
limits: No live TERMPoint or terminal appointment lookup is implemented.
A reported appointment does not establish that it is current, matches this movement, or will be accepted at the gate.

findings.label: Same-day transaction and gate release evidence
limits: The pinned release contains no retained source clause that establishes same-day transaction or gate-release requirements.
No live terminal transaction, gate, cargo-release, or admission integration is implemented. Reported release status cannot establish entry.
Synthetic development cases only; no operational entry or dispatch clearance.
Reported facts are not authoritative verification, even when a reporter says verified.
The catalog is incomplete; current policy, CDL, gate state and other duties remain outside executable coverage.
Archived directions and bulletins do not establish legal access or current road conditions.
Only APM induction has an executable evaluator, using server-owned synthetic fixtures.

findings.label: Trip, terminal, and timing context
limits: These facts select assessment scope; they do not establish dispatch, route, or entry clearance.

The catalog's terminal-specific evidence supports APM Elizabeth only. A missing terminal leaves applicability unresolved, and another terminal creates an unsupported-terminal coverage gap rather than an exemption.
The NJPASS-hosted route-review clause is retained evidence, but its official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

findings.label: Gross, axle, and spacing evidence
limits: The federal clause is limited to the Interstate system and reasonable access; the New Jersey single-axle clause is limited to non-Interstate New Jersey roads.
Which limit applies depends on the exact roadway jurisdiction and route. This catalog implements no bridge-formula, axle-group, tire-load, or legal-weight calculator.
Gross weight, axle count, and reported axle weights or spacings do not by themselves establish compliance.
The NJPASS-hosted route-review clause is excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

findings.label: Loaded dimensions and exact route access
limits: Width limits depend on route-network status, and the cited local-access rule is expressly limited to a 102-inch-wide standard truck using unrestricted local roads by the direct route.
A road's absence from a listed network or restriction table establishes neither permission nor prohibition. Current local postings and every segment still require verification.
Published terminal directions and stored route topology are not legal route designation, bridge-clearance evidence, or navigable truck-route approval.

findings.label: Permit type and load eligibility evidence
limits: Permit applicability depends on the load, dimensions, axle facts, trip time, and permit terms; no legal interpretation or permit-validity check is implemented.
The ocean-container sources concern sealed ocean-borne containers and do not make every container move eligible for that permit type.
The NJPASS-hosted permit clause is retained but excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently archived and compared.
A reported permit, including a reported-valid permit, is user-reported evidence and does not establish approval or route coverage.

findings.label: Cross-authority route and permit coverage
limits: A New Jersey State permit does not establish approval for toll, county, local, Port Authority, or terminal-controlled segments.
Every reported approval requires verification from the responsible authority; a complete set of user reports is not cross-authority clearance.
The retained toll-road approval clause is excluded from the verified graph because official code-of-record currentness was not independently verified.

findings.label: Current route postings and operating conditions
limits: No live current-policy, posting, closure, lane, detour, escort, or route-condition integration is implemented.
The archived Port Street bulletin is a quarantined dated observation, not a source clause or proof of conditions on the trip date; it must be rechecked before operational use.
A user-reported check time does not verify the result, authority, route coverage, or continued currentness of that check.

findings.label: DTR registration and vehicle RFID evidence
limits: No live PortTruckPass, DTR, ownership-amendment, or RFID lookup is implemented.
Reported DTR or RFID status is not registry verification and does not establish terminal entry.

findings.label: DTR engine-policy evidence and retained tariff conflict
limits: The release preserves an unresolved internal tension between Subrules 34-1101 and 34-1140; the deadline clause is explicitly excluded from verified use.
This catalog does not reconcile the tariff, infer enforcement, or categorically approve or deny a truck from engine model year alone.
The 2014 engine language concerns completing DTR registration and must not be silently converted into a universal terminal-entry rule.

findings.label: Driver TWIC evidence
limits: The federal clause concerns unescorted access to regulated secure areas and retains its stated exceptions; this catalog does not determine whether an exception applies.
No live TSA or Port Authority credential verification is implemented. A reported TWIC is not verified access authorization.

findings.label: SeaLink and TWIC registration evidence
limits: No live SeaLink or TWIC-registration lookup is implemented.
Possession of an identifier and a reported registration do not establish current validity or terminal entry.

findings.label: APM safety induction tied to the current SeaLink
limits: This is the only catalog requirement with an implemented check, and it uses server-owned synthetic evidence rather than a live training provider.
A matching synthetic result addresses only induction for the current SeaLink; it is not dispatch, route, permit, or terminal-entry clearance.
Archived policy is not verified as current for the trip, and synthetic assessment dates do not create a training-expiry rule.
No dispatch, entry, permit or route clearance is issued.
Archived policy has not been verified as current for this trip.
Synthetic evidence assessment dates are test controls, not a training expiry rule.
An out-of-scope check does not mean the person is exempt from other requirements.

findings.label: APM gate appointment evidence
limits: No live TERMPoint or terminal appointment lookup is implemented.
A reported appointment does not establish that it is current, matches this movement, or will be accepted at the gate.

findings.label: Same-day transaction and gate release evidence
limits: The pinned release contains no retained source clause that establishes same-day transaction or gate-release requirements.
No live terminal transaction, gate, cargo-release, or admission integration is implemented. Reported release status cannot establish entry.
Synthetic development cases only; no operational entry or dispatch clearance.
Reported facts are not authoritative verification, even when a reporter says verified.
The catalog is incomplete; current policy, CDL, gate state and other duties remain outside executable coverage.
Archived directions and bulletins do not establish legal access or current road conditions.
Only APM induction has an executable evaluator, using server-owned synthetic fixtures.
